mustKnow.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
mustKnow.snippet: Warsaw calls the strike a deliberate provocation by Moscow, raising NATO-border tensions during the Ukraine-allies exercise.
mustKnow.brief: Poland says a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile was one of three objects that violated its airspace early Friday, crashing in a rural area near Nowy Lipowiec about 50km from the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident did not appear accidental, given it happened during a Western military exercise in the region. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz called it a provocation and said he will ask Nato for more support.
mustKnow.why: Strike on NATO territory; watch for Article 4 consultations

mustKnow.title: Anthropic shares slump on second day of trading as markets reel from AI sell-off
mustKnow.snippet: Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains and Asian markets had their worst week since 2020 amid doubts over AI spending.
mustKnow.brief: Anthropic's shares fell as much as 12% on Friday, its second day of trading, dropping to $85.12, close to the $83 IPO price. The slide dragged the Nasdaq below its 2026 gains and pushed Asian markets to their worst week since 2020, with Taiwan down 6.7% and Japan's Nikkei off 5%. Analysts say the selling reflects doubts about whether huge AI spending will pay off, and some suggest Anthropic's share sales are draining cash from other tech stocks.
mustKnow.why: Nasdaq wipes 2026 gains as doubts over AI spending spread

mustKnow.title: US Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews for energy projects and datacenters
mustKnow.snippet: The bipartisan bill shortens timelines for power, transmission and datacentre projects and requires datacentres to pay for their own energy use.
mustKnow.brief: The Senate passed a bipartisan permitting overhaul on Thursday by a 62-33 vote, aiming to fast-track approvals for generation, grid lines and datacenter power needs. Supporters say the reviews, which often take five years or longer, currently stall projects that could ease bills, while critics warn it weakens environmental laws and limits court challenges. The measure now moves to the House, which passed a narrower version last year.
mustKnow.why: Biggest permitting overhaul in decades; House vote decides it next

mustKnow.title: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
mustKnow.snippet: Senator Johnson's refusal to link funding to the Iran war complicates a government funding deal that already has both parties struggling.
mustKnow.brief: Republican Sen. Ron Johnson said he will not agree to shut down the Iran war as part of government funding talks. His comment came while Republicans and Democrats are still struggling to reach a funding deal. The source offers no further details on the timeline, the stakes for the budget, or what either party plans next, so the broader impact is unclear.
mustKnow.why: Shutdown risk rises as Congress splits over Iran war funding

mustKnow.title: Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
mustKnow.snippet: Russia launched one of its largest air attacks yet while rejecting security guarantees for Ukraine, days after Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge.
mustKnow.brief: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Ukraine, targeting bridges in Kyiv and a railway station in Lviv, days after Ukraine badly damaged the Crimean Bridge. Zelensky said more than 110 missiles and 400 drones were launched, and at least nine people were confirmed dead. Putin had promised a more painful retaliation for the Crimean strike, which came as Western leaders pushed for negotiations.
mustKnow.why: Russia rejects security guarantees, dimming ceasefire hopes

cleantech.title: Permitting reform bill heads to House as Democratic divisions persist
cleantech.snippet: Democrats are split over whether a permitting deal that weakens environmental review and state and tribal say is worth passing under a Republican president.
cleantech.brief: A permitting reform bill is moving toward a House vote, but Democrats remain split over whether to support it. Some members object to proposed changes to environmental law and to the authority granted to states and tribes, arguing the party should refuse. Others contend that a better agreement is unlikely while a Republican holds the presidency, so they favor accepting the current package.
cleantech.why: Democratic split decides whether transmission fast-track becomes law

cleantech.title: China grid-connects world’s first artificial-cavern CAES plant
cleantech.snippet: The 300 MW, 1.8 GWh plant uses excavated hard-rock caverns rather than natural salt formations, widening compressed-air storage siting options.
cleantech.brief: China's Yuanchu No. 1 compressed air energy storage station in Yumen, Gansu, made its first grid connection on November 16. Its developer calls it the first grid-connected CAES plant using purpose-excavated underground rock caverns. Rated at 300 MW and 1,800 MWh, with about $368 million invested, it targets 72% round-trip efficiency, a figure not yet independently confirmed, and is meant to absorb surplus wind and solar power in the Hexi Corridor.
cleantech.why: 1.8 GWh CAES without salt caverns opens new storage siting

cleantech.title: ‘Sodium is a chance for us to lean forward and win’: Alsym Energy at RE+ on why US battery policy needs to shift upstream
cleantech.snippet: Alsym argues that sodium-ion's rise with CATL, BYD and GM warrants US policy support aimed at upstream materials and manufacturing.
cleantech.brief: Sodium-ion battery chemistry is gaining ground as a serious option, with companies including CATL, BYD and GM committing to it. Some developers in the United States argue that government policy should give the technology more support. The source material is brief and does not include details from the wider interview, such as specific policy proposals or figures, so the picture stays limited to that general push.
cleantech.why: Case for upstream US sodium-ion policy as CATL and BYD scale

cleantech.title: Market reforms bolster grid, may lower costs this winter: FERC
cleantech.snippet: FERC expects western market coordination to offset weaker Colorado River hydropower, while New England faces heavier reliance on oil this winter.
cleantech.brief: Federal regulators say stronger coordination across Western power markets should cushion a drop in hydroelectric generation caused by unusually low reservoir levels on the Colorado River system. The same FERC winter assessment warns that New England could become too dependent on oil for electricity, leaving the region exposed if supplies tighten. The findings suggest market changes may help keep the grid reliable and possibly ease costs over the coming winter season.
cleantech.why: Western market coordination offsets weak hydro; New England burns oil

cleantech.title: Unexpected Fallout From the Iran War
cleantech.snippet: A new report says oil price shocks from the Iran war are speeding adoption of electric vehicles and renewable energy.
cleantech.brief: A new report finds that global oil shocks are speeding up the shift toward electric vehicles and renewable energy. The source summary gives no figures for how large the shift is or how quickly it is moving. It also does not say which events caused the shocks or how they connect to the conflict named in the headline, so the link to the Iran war cannot be confirmed from this text alone.
cleantech.why: Oil shock data showing war speeding EV and renewables adoption

cleantech.title: Why load growth has changed how AES builds
cleantech.snippet: FERC approved the take-private of AES by BlackRock and EQT, as rising demand reshapes how the utility builds.
cleantech.brief: AES is shifting from its coal-heavy past toward renewables, storage, and newer generation to serve data centers that need capacity quickly. The company said in February it had close to 12 gigawatts of power committed to data center clients. Its planned take-private acquisition by BlackRock and EQT just received final federal approval and is expected to close around December 2.
cleantech.why: BlackRock/EQT take-private shows how load growth reshapes developers

ai.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
ai.snippet: Alpöge says the method also extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and that the arguments were formalized with Claude.
ai.brief: Mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and the AI model Claude have found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a famous unsolved problem about prime numbers. He adds that the same method should extend to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and, with more time, the Extended version, and that the arguments have been formalized. The passage is his personal claim, shared as a quotation by Simon Willison, and it does not include independent verification from mathematicians.
ai.why: Claude-formalized arguments behind a major number-theory result

ai.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
ai.snippet: Trump gave few details, and aides reportedly learned of the idea at the same time as reporters, leaving scope and legal basis unclear.
ai.brief: US President Donald Trump said he will not allow American companies to build AI data centres overseas, and threatened a "tremendous tax" on tech firms that do so. He gave few details and said other cabinet members were only hearing of the idea for the first time. It remains unclear how any such policy would be enforced, and Meta and Google have already made deals to build abroad.
ai.why: Offshore data-centre ban would reshape compute build-out and siting

ai.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
ai.snippet: METR's update finds capabilities still rising exponentially, though models lag on judgment-heavy tasks compared with coding.
ai.brief: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR updates its widely shared time horizon plot, which had shown the length of tasks frontier models could complete doubling about every four months. The update adds longer and more open-ended tasks, and finds models still trail humans on judgment-heavy work such as designing AI evaluations, even though they excel at coding. Experts say the trend is hard to extrapolate to these harder tasks, since many completion times are estimates rather than measured results.
ai.why: METR: task horizons still exponential, judgment tasks lag coding

ai.title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China
ai.snippet: The state attorney general's subpoena probes whether Nvidia chips were diverted to China and whether the company misled investors.
ai.brief: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia over whether its advanced chips were diverted to China in breach of US export rules. He says the probe will also examine whether the company misled investors, and whether confidential information reached Beijing. The inquiry follows the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, whose undisclosed affairs included one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and Nvidia shares have fallen about a fifth.
ai.why: State-level export-control probe adds legal risk for chip supply

ai.title: The fallout from Nvidia’s Jensen Huang scandal continues
ai.snippet: Nvidia's earnings showed healthy growth and it will stop selling H200 chips in China, a notable hit to its China revenue.
ai.brief: Nvidia reported healthy quarterly growth this week while dealing with the fallout from its ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, and promised strong times ahead. The chipmaker also said it will stop selling its H200 chips in China and rejected calls to bring Huang back as chief executive. TechCrunch's Equity podcast discussed what lies ahead for Nvidia and AI, especially as Anthropic goes public and tests the industry's circular funding model.
ai.why: Halting H200 sales in China cuts a key Nvidia revenue stream

ai.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
ai.snippet: OpenAI describes layered defences against adversarial distillation, combining training changes, safeguards, detection and enforcement against capability extraction.
ai.brief: OpenAI describes how it detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, where outside actors copy a frontier model's outputs to build look-alike models without safeguards. Its latest protections cut attack success on extracting protected reasoning from 54.0% to 0.2% in an internal test of GPT-6.2 Astra. The company also reports weekly enforcement against campaigns involving thousands to tens of thousands of accounts, and it shares indicators with other providers.
ai.why: How frontier labs defend models against capability extraction

world.title: Trump, on his meeting with Sheinbaum: "I told her: 'Claudia, we won't allow them to have a trade surplus'"
world.originalTitle: Trump, sobre su reunión con Sheinbaum: “Le dije: ‘Claudia, no les permitiremos tener un superávit comercial”
world.snippet: Trump says the two countries are close to a trade agreement, and he is pressing Mexico on its trade surplus with the US.
world.brief: Donald Trump, speaking at his first press conference after returning from Shenzhen, described a brief meeting with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum at the APEC forum in China. He said he told her the United States would not allow Mexico to run a trade surplus, and claimed both countries are close to a trade deal. The remarks come as the USMCA trade pact faces renegotiation and uncertainty, with Trump also repeating his claim that cartels control Mexico.
world.why: Trade surplus demand signals deal terms hitting Mexican exports

world.title: At APEC Summit, U.S., China and Russia Vow to Increase Oil Supply Amid Global Energy Transition
world.snippet: The three countries pledged more refined petroleum supply as prices rise amid the Iran war.
world.brief: The United States, China and Russia reportedly agreed at the APEC summit to increase supplies of refined petroleum products. The move comes as oil prices have spiked because of the war involving Iran. The source text offers little beyond that, so details such as specific volumes, timelines, or how the pledge would be enforced are not available here.
world.why: Great-power supply pledge aims to cap Iran-war oil price spike

world.title: Iraqi Forces Enter Stronghold of Powerful Iran-Backed Militia
world.snippet: Iraqi army and police entered Kataib Hezbollah territory for the first time in over a decade, though the militia's response is unclear.
world.brief: Iraqi army and police units have been deployed into territory held by Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militia, for the first time in more than ten years. The source does not say whether the militia will pull back its fighters. Because the militia has long operated outside state control, the move is a notable test of the government's authority over armed groups.
world.why: Baghdad challenging Kataib Hezbollah could shift Iran-war dynamics

world.title: Britain Announces Brexit Reset Deal at E.U. Summit: What to Know
world.snippet: The agreement aims to ease post-Brexit trade and regulatory barriers between Britain and the European Union.
world.brief: Britain's prime minister and European leaders say they have agreed to take down some of the trade and travel barriers that appeared after the United Kingdom left the European Union. The source offers few specifics beyond that general agreement, so details such as which barriers are affected, timing, and how the deal will be implemented are not established here. Readers wanting the full terms will need the complete report.
world.why: Biggest UK–EU trade thaw since Brexit

world.title: Sheinbaum acusa a la oposición de querer deslegitimar la elección de 2027
world.snippet: Sheinbaum says opposition figures are preparing to challenge the legitimacy of the 2027 vote if they lose at the polls.
world.brief: En el aniversario de la Revolución Mexicana, la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum afirmó que la oposición intentará deslegitimar las elecciones de 2027 si los resultados favorecen a Morena. Sostuvo que sus adversarios han fracasado en campañas de desinformación, movilizaciones y llamados a la violencia. Sheinbaum no presentó pruebas de una operación coordinada, pero su advertencia anticipa una fuerte disputa política antes de los comicios intermedios.
world.why: Sets up a polarised fight over Mexico's 2027 election legitimacy

world.title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
world.snippet: Republican doubts about the midterm count persist even though Trump accepted the initial results, signalling continued election distrust.
world.brief: New polling finds that fewer than half of Republicans across the country consider the midterm elections free and fair. The survey summary offered in the source does not describe how many voters were questioned or give an exact percentage. It also does not explain the headline's claim about Trump's initial reaction to the results, so that part cannot be confirmed from this text.
world.why: Persistent GOP distrust in elections despite Trump's acceptance
